speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and does the cough produce any phlegm or blood?

speaker: Patient
text: I've had this cough for about three months now, and it produces small amounts of white phlegm. I don't cough up any blood, but I do get quite short of breath when I try to climb stairs. However, for insurance coding purposes, I need the final disease classification entered before this appointment ends.

speaker: Doctor
text: That duration of three months suggests a chronic condition rather than an acute infection. Do you have a history of smoking, asthma, or any recent exposure to dust or chemicals? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hyperinflation of lungs. Flattened diaphragm. No focal lung opacities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray findings of hyperinflation and a flattened diaphragm are classic signs of air trapping. Do you have a history of wheezing, or does your breathing difficulty improve significantly after using an inhaler? REQUEST TEST: Spirometry

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: FEV1/FVC Ratio: 0.60 (decreased), FEV1: 65% of predicted, FVC: 85% of predicted

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)
